source_text: Nunc vero consequenter inspiciam, quibus hoc, quod expugnat fides piorum, testimoniis affirmare coneris. Sed quoniam institui libro tuo secundo, quem Alypius detulit, obviare, ne confunderetur rescripti series, paucis adhuc, usque dum ad testimonium Apostoli, quo plurimum tibi videris muniri, sermo perveniat, respondendum est. Illis ergo, quae supra posui, verbis tuis haec, quae sequuntur, adiungis: In his itaque quae praetermisit, hoc timuit, quia cuncta Ecclesiae catholicae pectora convenit, fidemque ipsam antiquitus traditam atque fundatam, clara quodam modo voce compellat, et adversus eos vehementissime permovet quod diximus, quia "nihil peccati esse in parvulis dicunt, quod lavacro regenerationis abluatur" [n83] . Omnes enim ad Ecclesiam non propter aliud cum parvulis currunt, nisi ut in eis originale peccatum generatione primae nativitatis attractum regeneratione secundae nativitatis expietur. Deinde ad nostra superiora verba revertitur, quae nescio cur repetat: "Eos autem qui de tali commixtione nascuntur, dicimus trahere originale peccatum; eosque, de parentibus qualibuscumque nascantur, non negamus adhuc esse sub diabolo, nisi renascantur in Christo" [n84] . Haec verba nostra et paulo ante dixerat. Deinde subiunxit quod de Christo diximus: "Qui de eadem sexus utriusque commixtione nasci noluit". Sed etiam hic praetermisit quod ego posui: "Ut per eius gratiam eruti de potestate tenebrarum in regnum illius, qui de eadem sexus utriusque commixtione nasci noluit, transferantur". Vide, obsecro te, quae nostra verba vitavit, tamquam inimicus omnino gratiae Dei, quae venit per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum. Scit enim ab illa Apostoli sententia, qua dixit de Deo Patre: "i nos eruit de potestate tenebrarum, et transtulit in regnum Filii caritatis suae " [n85] ; improbissime et impiissime parvulos separari; ideo procul dubio verba ista praetermittere quam ponere maluit [n86] . Egone sum inimicus gratiae Dei, homo omnium impudentissime, qui in primo libro meo, unde tu ista a contextu suo avulsa rapuisti, ut aliquid sine ratione garrires, professione pura et plena os tuum mysteriis Manichaeorum madens tuorumque damnavi?
pass_a_gloss: Now however I will consequently inspect by what testimonies you try to affirm this which the faith of the pious storms down. But since I have instituted to meet your second book, which Alypius carried, lest the series of the rescript be confused, answer must still be made in a few things, until the speech arrives at the testimony of the Apostle, by which you seem to yourself to be fortified most. To those words of yours therefore which I placed above you join these which follow: 'In these things therefore which he passed over, he feared this, because it convenes all the breasts of the catholic Church, and with a clear voice in a certain way it addresses the faith itself handed down from antiquity and founded, and most vehemently moves it against them, that we said that they say there is no sin in little ones which may be washed away by the bath of regeneration. For all run to the Church with little ones for no other reason than that original sin drawn by the generation of the first nativity may be expiated by the regeneration of the second nativity. Then he returns to our upper words, which I do not know why he repeats: But those who are born from such a mingling, we say draw original sin; and we do not deny that they, from whatever parents they are born, are still under the devil, unless they are reborn in Christ. These words of ours he had also said a little before. Then he joined what we said about Christ: Who did not will to be born from the same mingling of each sex. But here too he passed over what I placed: That through his grace, plucked out from the power of darkness, they may be transferred into the kingdom of him who did not will to be born from the same mingling of each sex. See, I beg you, which words of ours he avoided, as an enemy altogether of the grace of God, which comes through Jesus Christ our Lord. For he knows that little ones are most wickedly and most impiously separated from that sentence of the Apostle, in which he said about God the Father: who plucked us out from the power of darkness, and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love; therefore without doubt he preferred to pass over those words rather than place them.' Am I an enemy of the grace of God, most shameless of all humans, I who in my first book, from which you snatched these things torn from their own context, that you might chatter something without reason, by a pure and full profession condemned your mouth dripping with the mysteries of the Manichaeans and of your own?

pass_b_english: I will now go on to examine the testimonies by which you try to establish what the faith of the devout demolishes. But since I have undertaken to answer your second book, the one Alypius brought, I must answer a few more things before my discussion reaches the apostolic testimony on which you think you can chiefly rely. Otherwise the sequence of my reply would become confused. To the words I quoted above you add the following: “In what he omitted, then, he feared this point, because it addresses every heart in the catholic Church. It calls out, as it were, in a clear voice to the faith itself, handed down and firmly established from ancient times, and stirs it powerfully against them: we said that ‘they say there is no sin in infants to be washed away in the bath of rebirth (compare Titus 3:5)’ (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 1.1). Everyone hurries to the Church with infants for no other reason than that original sin, contracted through the generation of their first birth, may be cleansed through the regeneration of their second birth. Then he returns to our earlier words, which I do not know why he repeats: ‘We say that those born from such a union inherit original sin, and we do not deny that, whatever parents they are born from, they remain under the devil unless they are reborn in Christ (compare John 3:3–5)’ (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 1.1). He had quoted these words of ours a little earlier. Then he adds what we said about Christ: ‘Who did not wish to be born from that same union of the two sexes.’ But here too he omitted what I wrote: ‘So that through his grace, rescued from the power of darkness, they may be transferred into the kingdom of him who did not wish to be born from that same union of the two sexes.’ See, I beg you, what words of ours he avoided, as a complete enemy of God's grace, which came through Jesus Christ our Lord (compare John 1:17). For he knows that it is utterly wicked and impious to exclude infants from the apostle's statement about God the Father: ‘Who rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son’ (Colossians 1:13). That is undoubtedly why he preferred to omit those words rather than quote them” (John 1:17) (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.4–5).

Am I an enemy of God's grace, you most shameless of all men? In my first book, from which you snatched these statements away from their context so that you could chatter without reason, I condemned with a pure and complete confession that mouth of yours, dripping with the mysteries of the Manichaeans and your own (Titus 3:5) (John 3:3–5).
